papers.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM

summary.tldr: TurboVLA introduces a direct V+L to A mapping, bypassing LLM-centric VLA pathways, achieving real-time performance and high success rates with reduced computational and memory overhead.
key_points: TurboVLA reformulates the VLA pathway from V to L to A to a direct V + L to A mapping.
It independently encodes visual observations and language instructions, using lightweight bidirectional vision-language interaction.
The model predicts continuous action chunks with a compact decoder.
TurboVLA achieves 97.7% average success on LIBERO with 0.2B parameters, 31.2 ms inference latency, and 0.9 GB VRAM on an RTX 4090.
This performance matches or outperforms larger LLM-centric VLA policies.
summary.why_it_matters: This design enables efficient robotic manipulation by significantly reducing computational and memory costs for VLA inference on consumer-grade hardware.

papers.title: DistillAlign: Coordinating Mode Covering and Mode Seeking in Autoregressive Video Distillation

summary.tldr: DistillAlign introduces joint distillation for autoregressive video, combining mode-seeking Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with a mode-covering Consistency Distillation constraint to improve generation quality, coverage, and diversity by addressing distributional misalignment.
key_points: Existing autoregressive video distillation methods decouple initialization and DMD stages, pursuing different target distributions and often judging by visual scores like VBench.
A distributional evaluation protocol measuring precision and coverage in a shared latent space reveals that high visual scores can mask low mode coverage, leading to suboptimal refinement.
The mode-seeking nature of reverse-KL in DMD can reduce coverage and diversity by driving the student to high-probability teacher regions in late training.
DistillAlign proposes joint distillation, integrating DMD's mode-seeking objective with a Consistency Distillation-based mode-covering constraint.
The method improves generation quality, coverage, and diversity, outperforming baselines refined with a Wan-14B teacher even when using a Wan-1.3B DMD teacher.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves autoregressive video distillation efficiency and quality by optimizing distributional alignment, allowing smaller models to achieve performance comparable to or better than larger models.

papers.title: CoRT: Counterfactual Replay for Token-Level Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: CoRT introduces a token-level credit weighting method for rubric-conditioned GRPO using counterfactual replay to redistribute response-level advantages without an auxiliary scorer.
key_points: CoRT addresses the uniform broadcasting of response-level rewards in GRPO by providing token-level credit allocation for rubric-based language model training.
The method uses counterfactual replay to rescore sampled responses under both rubric-conditioned and criteria-free prompts, generating tokenwise log-likelihood contrasts.
These contrasts are mapped to bounded, response-normalized weights, which redistribute the signed GRPO advantage across tokens.
CoRT improves over response-level GRPO by an average of 4.4 percentage points and competes with learned token-level credit baselines without a separate relevance-learning stage.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances the precision of reinforcement learning for language models by enabling fine-grained credit assignment within responses, improving training efficiency and performance.

papers.title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?

summary.tldr: HumanCLAW is a new evaluation framework that decouples VLM action decision-making from low-level motor execution, revealing current VLMs lack embodied self-awareness in physical interaction.
key_points: HumanCLAW evaluates VLMs by having them issue atomic skill commands translated into sub-second, continuous full-body motion with real physical consequences, factoring out execution-side disturbances.
The framework measures a model's action intelligence by focusing on its moment-to-moment choice of what the body should execute next.
HumanCLAW-Bench comprises 1,218 long-horizon, egocentric find-navigate-interact episodes across 41 indoor scenes.
Nine state-of-the-art VLMs were tested, with the best achieving only a 16.8% success rate.
Current VLMs fail due to a lack of embodied self-awareness, losing track of their own body's position, goal proximity, or obstacle collisions.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a clearer method to assess VLM decision-making in embodied AI, highlighting critical limitations in current models' understanding of their own physical state.

papers.title: DecoEvo: Score-Decoupled Co-Evolution of Solver and Rubric-Generator Skills in Text Space

summary.tldr: DecoEvo introduces a novel method for text-space optimization by co-evolving solver and rubric-generator skills with decoupled objectives, addressing limitations of fixed or solver-score-dependent evaluation in open-ended tasks.
key_points: DecoEvo co-evolves a solver skill and a rubric-generator skill using decoupled objectives without gold rubrics.
The solver skill is updated via criterion-level feedback.
The rubric-generator skill is revised through audits of requirement coverage and response discrimination, independent of aggregate solver score.
This decoupling focuses generator updates on newly exposed solver weaknesses, avoiding repeated emphasis on satisfied criteria.
DecoEvo achieves 2.8–5.0% relative gains over SkillOpt across five benchmarks and three LLM backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves LLM optimization in open-ended tasks by enabling more robust and comprehensive evaluation evolution, leading to better performance.

papers.title: CLBench-V: Evaluating Multimodal Context Learning from Grounding to Knowledge Acquisition

summary.tldr: CLBench-V is a new benchmark for multimodal context learning, evaluating models across context grounding, new information application, and new knowledge learning, revealing current models are far from saturated.
key_points: CLBench-V organizes tasks around three dimensions: context grounding, new information application, and new knowledge learning to localize where context use breaks down.
The benchmark combines converted public benchmarks with newly constructed datasets spanning science, finance, long-document understanding, spatial reasoning, and web-based VQA.
Automated construction and filtering procedures were used for newly built datasets to reduce task creation cost.
Across 3,443 instances and six multimodal models, the best overall score achieved was 0.2847, indicating significant room for improvement.
InternVL3.5-30B-A3B performed best on context grounding and new knowledge learning, while Qwen3.5-Plus excelled in new information application.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark highlights the current limitations of multimodal models in learning from diverse contextual information, which is crucial for real-world applications.

papers.title: CAST: Game Solvers as Turn-Level Teachers for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: CAST converts game solver state value changes into turn-level solver advantages, improving LLM agent performance in long-horizon games by providing denser credit assignment signals for reinforcement learning.
key_points: CAST utilizes changes in a game solver's state value to generate turn-level signals, addressing the sparsity of final rewards in RLVR for LLM agents.
The method injects these value changes as solver advantages into RLVR, providing denser process signals for credit assignment.
Under a soft-optimal solver assumption, maximizing solver advantage is equivalent to on-policy distillation from the solver using only scalar values.
CAST outperformed all trained baselines across Sokoban, Minesweeper, and Rush Hour in both in-domain and unseen-difficulty evaluations.
The approach achieved the highest average zero-shot performance on ALFWorld and WebShop.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a scalable and effective way to train LLM agents for complex, long-horizon decision-making tasks by providing more informative turn-level feedback.

papers.title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution

summary.tldr: SkillRise is a unified reinforcement learning framework for LLM agents that learns and curates transferable skills across progressively challenging, related tasks.
key_points: SkillRise uses a single policy to alternate between task solving and curating an evolving skill document passed to the next task.
Decoupled credit assignment supervises task solving with current outcomes and curation with discounted downstream outcomes.
SkillRise achieved Pass@1 performance gains of 2.3 to 8.5 percentage points over the strongest baseline on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld.
Performance improves with longer sequences of related tasks, indicating transferable skill reuse rather than repeated sampling benefits.
SkillRise substantially reduces runtime overhead compared to multi-stage skill learning pipelines.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides an efficient method for LLM agents to extract, refine, and reuse transferable skills across diverse tasks.

papers.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis

summary.tldr: MindForge is an automated pipeline converting open-source command-line programs into source-free environments for training small language models in whole-life-cycle software engineering, significantly improving their program synthesis capabilities.
key_points: MindForge creates source-free training environments from open-source command-line programs, exposing only a compiled executable and documentation, addressing the lack of scalable training environments for from-scratch program synthesis.
A data recipe of program synthesis trajectories was curated using GLM-5.2 as the teacher agent, derived from repositories disjoint from ProgramBench.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-27B on these trajectories increased its ProgramBench average test pass rate from 37.98% to 49.51%.
The fine-tuned model showed absolute gains across seven unseen software engineering benchmarks, including 31.00 points on RepoZero-C2Rust and 14.16 on DeepSWE.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables smaller language models to achieve performance comparable to larger frontier models in complex software engineering tasks, making advanced code generation more accessible.

papers.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch

summary.tldr: SpecFirst is a two-stage framework that improves LLM-based program synthesis from scratch by separating behavioral specification elicitation from code synthesis, resolving ambiguities and providing a stable reference.
key_points: SpecFirst decomposes program synthesis into a specification elicitation stage by a dedicated spec agent and a subsequent code synthesis stage by a separate agent.
The framework was evaluated on all 200 ProgramBench instances across four models, showing a 6.9%-21.3% improvement in test pass rates.
Binary exploration coverage improved by 9.4%-18.5% with SpecFirst compared to single-loop baselines.
Behavioral analysis indicates that a prior specification enables earlier and more sustained code construction.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach significantly enhances the ability of LLM-based agents to construct programs from scratch, addressing a major limitation in current software engineering tasks.

papers.title: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation

summary.tldr: StatePlay is a novel state-aware game world model that jointly predicts visual content and game states to promote mechanics-consistent generation, improving fidelity by 18.6% over models without explicit state modeling.
key_points: StatePlay utilizes a mixture-of-transformers (MoT)-style architecture to preserve specialized visual and state representations while enabling cross-modal interaction.
The model guides frame generation using predicted game states, with each branch optimized via distinct, modality-suited objectives.
StatePlay achieves an average normalized L1 distance below 0.06 for state prediction.
The method improves mechanics fidelity in generated game rollouts by 18.6% compared to models lacking explicit state modeling.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach advances game world models beyond pixel-level realism to generate mechanically faithful and consistent game environments.

papers.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies

summary.tldr: This paper introduces "shadow evaluations" where AI agents attempt to answer open-ended research questions from unpublished papers, with original authors grading the output.
key_points: Frontier AI agents were given six days and thousands of dollars of compute to address central research questions from two unpublished NeurIPS 2026 submissions.
Agents completed all engineering tasks autonomously but failed to make substantial progress on the research questions, leading to unambiguous rejection by authors.
Identified five recurring failure modes: poor judgment for publishable research, uncreative responses to design shortcomings, ineffective backtracking, poor resource awareness, and instruction drift.
A robustness check with a second model and scaffold replicated these observed failures.
summary.why_it_matters: Current AI agents can handle engineering aspects of AI research but lack critical capabilities for open-ended research questions, limiting full automation of AI R&D.

papers.title: OVEarth-Bench: Evaluating Category Breadth and Query Diversity for Open-Vocabulary Earth Observation

summary.tldr: OVEarth-Bench is a new benchmark for open-vocabulary Earth observation, extending evaluation with broad hierarchical category coverage and diverse query forms for mask and box localization.
key_points: OVEarth-Bench evaluates open-vocabulary Earth observation by extending category breadth with hierarchical coverage (positive/negative expressions) and query diversity (vocabulary, referring, reasoning queries).
The benchmark supports mask and box localization under a unified zero-shot protocol.
Evaluation shows current methods have limited performance, MLLM-based methods achieve the strongest overall performance, and EO-specific methods generally underperform general models.
Broader category coverage in OVEarth-Bench yields more stable model rankings.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides guidance for future open-vocabulary EO method design by highlighting the need for more realistic, diverse, and high-quality benchmarks.

papers.title: Memory for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: This survey introduces a systematic, architecture-centric taxonomy that categorizes large language model memory mechanisms across representation, update dynamics, and persistence axes.
key_points: Taxonomy classifies LLM memory along three orthogonal axes: representation (implicit vs. explicit), update dynamics (offline vs. online), and persistence (short-term vs. long-term).
Formalizes granular memory operations including writing, routing, state transitions, and consolidation.
Delineates boundaries between computation-coupled memory and independently addressable memory across diverse strategies like transient attention, recurrent state dynamics, and scalable lookups.
Analyzes hybrid memory architectures, system-level efficiency trade-offs, and multi-dimensional evaluation methodologies.
summary.why_it_matters: By unifying fragmented memory mechanisms into a cohesive framework, the survey provides a principled foundation for designing scalable, adaptive, and memory-centric LLM architectures.

papers.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding

summary.tldr: OmegaUse-OfficeVal is a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on 100 long-horizon office-suite tasks, incorporating economic grounding with human labor time and task price proxies.
key_points: The benchmark includes 100 office-suite tasks, derived from practitioner requests, requiring an average of 2.32 hours of human labor.
Each task is paired with human labor time and a task price proxy, enabling value-weighted evaluation and cost comparisons between human and LLM inference.
Code-based verifiers, developed from fine-grained rubrics, ensure stable evaluation of task completion.
Evaluated frontier LLMs are substantially cheaper and faster than human workers but have not yet achieved human-level deliverable quality.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a method to evaluate LLM agents for office tasks based on both performance and economic viability, highlighting current limitations in quality despite cost advantages.

papers.title: Voice Memory for Agentic Speech Recognition

summary.tldr: Voice Memory is an inference-only agentic speech recognition scheme using a frozen corrector and a per-domain memory, reducing over-correction and improving weighted word error rate.
key_points: Voice Memory employs a listener-thinker architecture where a frozen corrector reads a per-domain memory to decide on hypothesis correction or abstention.
A score-gated optimizer asynchronously revises the memory file, accepting edits only if they strictly improve a held-out score.
The system reduces generative error correction over-correction from 64% to 35% on financial news.

Voice Memory lowers weighted word error rate from 8.36% to 7.52% across ten HyPoradise domains, with significant gains in air-travel commands (8.40% to 3.40%) and noisy far-field speech (12.69% to 10.46%).
The memory adds zero parameters to the inference path and transfers across corrector families.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a practical method for improving speech recognition accuracy and robustness without increasing inference complexity or requiring model retraining.

papers.title: Explicit Layer Modeling for Video Object Insertion and Layer Decomposition

summary.tldr: TriLayer dataset and DBL-Diffusion framework introduce explicit layer modeling for video object insertion and layer decomposition using aligned RGB composite, background, and RGBA foreground triplets.
key_points: TriLayer provides a large-scale video dataset with aligned composite, background, and RGBA foreground layers that capture appearance and visual effects.
DBL-Diffusion utilizes a dual-branch architecture that jointly processes RGB composites and RGBA foregrounds via shared denoising and cross-branch interaction.
DBL-Insert generates explicit RGBA layers to facilitate realistic compositing and flexible post-editing.
DBL-Decompose recovers distinct foreground and background layers directly using explicit triplet supervision instead of per-scene optimization.
summary.why_it_matters: Explicit layer supervision eliminates reliance on per-scene optimization and implicit inference, enabling accurate video object compositing, decomposition, and downstream post-editing.

papers.title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale

summary.tldr: GPT-Red is an automated red-teaming agent trained via a scalable self-play algorithm against diverse defender agents to discover novel prompt injection attacks in frontier LLMs.
key_points: Trained using a self-play algorithm where the attacker targets a diverse, simultaneously-trained population of defender agents in realistic environments.
Utilized RL post-training compute on par with OpenAI's largest runs, marking the largest documented LLM safety training run.
Adversarially trained GPT-5.6, while reliably breaking prior models up to GPT-5.5 and outperforming human red-teamers.
Demonstrated generalization to held-out environments, defender models, and test harnesses, establishing a self-improvement flywheel for safety.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated, large-scale discovery of prompt injection vulnerabilities that surpass human red-teaming capabilities to robustify production frontier models.

papers.title: CADENCE: Closing the Reasoning Gap via Coverage-Adaptive On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: CADENCE is a distillation framework that closes LLM reasoning gaps using adaptive divergence scheduling, entropy-based gradient boosts, partial-credit dense rewards, and low-compute execution.
key_points: Features DRIFT, which uses per-token convex mixtures of forward-KL and reverse-KL surrogate objectives on student-sampled trajectories.
Includes COVA for coverage-adaptive divergence transitions, FTB for concentrating gradients at high-entropy forking tokens, and CCD for partial-credit rewards on incorrect-but-close traces.
Extends capabilities via LAP length-preference reinforcement, EMR entropy-matching calibration, and BSD bootstrapped self-distillation.
Achieves 72.1% GSM8K pass@1 when distilling a 0.5B student from a 3B teacher, closing 76.2% of the reasoning gap.
Runs completely on modest consumer hardware using a single Apple Mac Studio with 64GB unified memory.
summary.why_it_matters: CADENCE proves that principled, coverage-adaptive distillation techniques can significantly improve compact model reasoning without requiring datacenter-scale training infrastructure.

papers.title: SecRespond: Benchmarking AI Agents for Real-World Post-Compromise Incident Response

summary.tldr: SecRespond is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on post-compromise incident response workflows using forensic disk snapshots and security product reports from real cloud environments.
key_points: Evaluates agents on generating forensic reports and remediation plans using forensic disk snapshots, alerts, vulnerability scans, and baseline checks.
Instantiated across 10 cyber ranges from compromised cloud hosts, covering 4 entry-point types, 21 ATT&CK techniques, and 5 operating systems.
Evaluated 23 frontier LLMs using the OpenCode agent harness.
Zero models achieved complete detection and remediation on any single cyber range due to failures in identifying silent intrusions and generating verified remediation plans.
summary.why_it_matters: It reveals critical limitations in current frontier LLMs for real-world security operations, specifically their inability to proactively investigate unalerted intrusions or execute complete post-compromise remediations.

papers.title: πR^2: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies

summary.tldr: πR^2 enables fast, closed-loop execution for flow-based manipulation policies by splitting conditioning into fast and slow channels and using a latency-adaptive flow schedule for single-step denoising.
key_points: Splits policy conditioning into a fast, per-tick proprioception channel and an asynchronous, slow vision-language feature channel.
Uses a latency-adaptive flow schedule based on diffusion forcing that treats in-flight actions as inpainting conditioning and outputs actions in one denoising step.
Finetuned from pretrained policies with minimal architectural changes, achieving ~25Hz closed-loop replanning (40ms fresh observation updates) on an NVIDIA A5000 GPU with GR00T-N1.7.
Increases task success rates over baseline models by up to 23% in simulation and 30% on real-world xArm6+XHand hardware.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the latency trade-off in action-chunking flow policies, allowing large vision-language-action models to perform real-time, closed-loop control on physical robots.

papers.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents

summary.tldr: StealthBench is a new benchmark that evaluates operational stealth in autonomous offensive-security agents across six OPSEC dimensions using 14 dockerized task scenarios and a 3-model LLM judge panel.
key_points: Derived from 11 hand-verified real-world OPSEC incidents (e.g., embedding credentials in public uploads, deleting production resources) expanded into 14 dockerized scenarios.
Evaluates agent trajectories using a 3-model LLM judge panel with majority-vote aggregation across three core metrics: safe success rate, Stealth@Solve, and reckless solve rate.
Benchmarking revealed systematic OPSEC failures across model families, with no model exceeding a 54% safe success rate (requiring both task completion and stealth).
summary.why_it_matters: Autonomous security agents frequently blow their cover during penetration tests, highlighting the need for OPSEC-aware agent development and automated monitoring before deploying them in live environments.

papers.title: Grading the Narrators: An Isnad-Rijal Framework for Claim-Level Provenance in Multi-Agent Knowledge Systems

summary.tldr: A multi-agent framework adapts Islamic hadith science (isnad-rijal) to assign graded, domain-specific narrator reliability to claim transmission chains, using weakest-link evaluation, content criticism, and automated routing.
key_points: Formalizes a mapping of hadith concepts (isnad transmission chains, rijal narrator grading, matn content criticism) to multi-agent AI knowledge pipelines.
Implements a relational schema for claim chains and narrator registries, paired with a decision matrix combining chain grades and content criticism for serve/review/quarantine routing.
Validated on 20,000 physics textbook claims, confirming weakest-link quarantine and independent-chain corroboration.

Identified limitations: a partial failure in the grade-recovery loop that missed the highest-fault narrator, and an inconclusive matched-coverage comparison due to reference content critic constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured methodology for tracking, evaluating, and filtering claims in autonomous multi-agent systems where knowledge degrades across multi-step LLM transformations.

papers.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications

summary.tldr: AISPA is a user-centric framework for auditing system prompts in AI applications, analyzing 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial products across eight user-centric dimensions.
key_points: AISPA evaluates system prompt instructions along eight user-centric dimensions, classifying them as protective or problematic.

An audit of 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products revealed significant variation in protective instruction adoption, with some organizations averaging over 60 protective instructions per product and others fewer than 5.
98.9% of products contained at least one protective instruction, but only 24% covered all eight AISPA dimensions.
Approximately 40% of products contained at least one problematic instruction, often coexisting with protective instructions within the same prompt.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings highlight the need for increased transparency, standardization, and independent oversight of system prompts in commercial AI products to address trust and accountability gaps.

papers.title: CDAE: Enhancing Perturbation Robustness in Pretrained Language Models with Contrastive Denoising

summary.tldr: CDAE enhances pretrained BERT embeddings by jointly optimizing contrastive and reconstruction objectives to learn perturbation-invariant representations, improving robustness against semantic-preserving textual perturbations.
key_points: CDAE refines pretrained BERT embeddings using a lightweight Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder.
The framework optimizes both contrastive and reconstruction objectives to achieve perturbation-invariant representations.
CDAE was evaluated against original BERT embeddings and SimCSE using multiple perturbation strategies of varying strengths.
Experimental results show CDAE consistently preserves higher embedding similarity under perturbations.
The source code for CDAE is publicly available on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves the stability of sentence embeddings, making them more reliable for downstream tasks despite minor textual variations.

papers.title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations

summary.tldr: Fairness Pruning identifies and prunes specific neurons in GLU-MLP layers that process demographic bias, demonstrating dissociable circuits for bias and model capabilities.
key_points: Fairness Pruning uses minimally contrastive prompt pairs and inference-time activation capture to locate neurons reacting differentially to demographic attributes in GLU architectures.
The method evaluates the signal at the down_proj input of GLU-MLP layers.
Zeroing identified neurons (up to 40 in Llama-3.2-1B, <0.031% of MLP width) alters demographic bias responses, but causes bidirectional bias destabilization due to mixed neuron effects.
The intervention retains 99.49% of reasoning and general knowledge capabilities in Llama-3.2-1B.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a surgical approach to locate and intervene on demographic bias, paving the way for targeted bias mitigation without significant performance degradation.

papers.title: Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing

summary.tldr: This paper introduces "coherent overlap" in MoE routing, where selected experts from a shared geometric neighborhood provide useful multi-expert computation despite substantial subspace overlap, challenging geometric complementarity.
key_points: Expert Subspace Separation Index (ESSI), matched-route residuals, and a prefix-controlled 2x2 factorial were used to distinguish route coherence, candidate quality, and candidate-by-context interaction.
Across six MoE architectures, expert subspaces overlap substantially, yet actual routes explain token representations better than matched alternatives.

In 39 factorial cells across OLMoE, Mixtral, and DeepSeek, the selected candidate explains more residual representation than unselected rivals, but the actual prefix narrows this advantage (all interactions negative).

Adding later experts improved next-token prediction in 24 of 39 frozen-route comparisons, and a controlled training study favored Top-2 over Top-1 in all three seeds, indicating functional value despite geometric narrowing.

The concept of "coherent overlap" describes routing selecting token-relevant experts from a shared geometric neighborhood where useful multi-expert computation persists without disjoint linear coverage.
summary.why_it_matters: Clarifying coherent overlap helps understand MoE functionality beyond geometric similarity, impacting redundancy assessment and pruning strategies.

papers.title: From Expert Reduction to Behavioral Divergence: Tracing Numerical State through Sparse MoE Inference

summary.tldr: Mathematically equivalent expert-reduction orders in sparse MoE can cause divergent execution and behavioral outcomes, even with frozen local MoE state.
key_points: DeepSeek-V4-Flash exhibits behavioral divergence across 720 A-mode orders (10 continuation basins) and 720 B-mode orders (360 structural classes, 11 basins) at one layer-5 fork.

B-mode orders under a Chinese prompt split into 202 layoffs, 113 hiring, and 45 other continuations, with maximum-L-infinity B-branch selection separating 12, 24, and 36 of 50 prompts by 8, 16, and 32 tokens.

P32, A, and B schemes alter native-reference route trajectories, while C preserves routes, token sequences, and texts, with a C check matching native MoE, post-mHC, next-router, and LM states bitwise.
Exact FP64 reconstruction of a B branch's full persistent state yields agreement for 301 downstream post-mHC states, checkpoints, routes, predictions, and text over seven steps.
Post-mHC is identified as an intra-token boundary and full persistent state as a cross-token continuation boundary, indicating divergence can survive token boundaries.
summary.why_it_matters: Expert operand conversion, accumulator precision, and reduction order are critical for numerical compatibility in sparse-MoE runtimes and hardware backends.

papers.title: Understanding Is Done Early: A Depth Division of Labor in Large Language Models and Its Use for Unbounded-Context Memory

summary.tldr: CoMem leverages a depth-based division of labor in LLMs for unbounded-context memory, achieving improved long-context performance and efficiency by caching and recomputing only upper layers.
key_points: CoMem writes context chunks through an intermediate layer, retrieves a fixed number of cached residual states, and recomputes only query-conditioned upper layers.
For a fixed retrieval budget, CoMem's model-side read compute and memory are independent of stored-context length.
CoMem achieved 97.05 on RULER and 38.27 on LoCoMo, outperforming full-context KV-Direct (34.59).
An adapter-free CoMem on an NVIDIA H20 at 128k context used 18.26 GB RAM (vs. 89.36 GB) and achieved a 7.83x prefill speedup.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a memory-efficient approach to extend LLM context windows, significantly reducing computational and memory overhead for long-context tasks.

papers.title: Can Agents Deceive? Evaluating Reasoning and Deception in ParliamentBench using a Social Deduction Game

summary.tldr: ParliamentBench, an open-source benchmark based on Secret Hitler, evaluates 16 LLMs' deceptive capabilities, reasoning, and persuasion in social deduction scenarios, revealing frontier models' strong performance but general struggle with deceptive consistency.
key_points: ParliamentBench evaluates 16 LLMs across 1,600 simulated matches in Secret Hitler, playing against each other and humans.
Three novel metrics were introduced to isolate social deduction, reasoning, and deceptive consistency.
Frontier models (GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.5, Grok 4.1 Fast, DeepSeek 3.1 Terminus) achieved strong performance in cooperative and deceptive roles.
Most LLMs struggled with deceptive consistency, with deception retention dropping below 50% throughout a game.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding LLM deceptive capabilities is crucial for safety when deploying them in high-stakes applications like medical and legal systems.

papers.title: PCAP-LM: An LLM-Native Text Representation for TLS Bulk Traffic Analysis

summary.tldr: PCAP-LM is an LLM-native text representation for TLS bulk traffic analysis that uses PacketGlyphs and BPE to achieve significant size reduction and improve LLM accuracy for forensic question-answering.
key_points: PCAP-LM transcodes raw network captures into semantic summaries using PacketGlyphs, an ASCII alphabet encoding packet direction, TCP/TLS state, log-scale size, and inter-packet delay.
A constrained PMI-BPE tokenizer and motif run-length encoding are applied to aggressively collapse repetitive behavioral patterns.

The method achieves an 812x size reduction over tshark -V, fitting entire captures within a single LLM context window, with a BPE vocabulary saturating at 159 tokens for 5G/4G TLS 1.3 bulk-download traffic.
In forensic question-answering, a frontier LLM achieved 99.3% accuracy with PCAP-LM documents, compared to 51.0% with a token-budget-matched tshark -V prefix.
The lossy design introduces a 24% false-negative rate for TCP retransmissions and requires vocabulary retraining for heterogeneous mixed-protocol environments.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables LLMs to effectively analyze large network traffic captures by reducing verbosity and improving accuracy in forensic tasks.

papers.title: RepBench: Compiling Benchmarks into Capability Representations for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: RepBench introduces a benchmark-grounded data layer for capability-aligned representation probing, compiling 13,427 benchmark papers and 353 datasets into 46,149 audited probe texts covering 94 capabilities.
key_points: RepBench established a taxonomy of 182 capability clusters across 13 families by crawling 13,427 benchmark papers.
The benchmark integrates 353 public datasets, yielding 46,149 audited probe texts for 94 capabilities, each supported by at least two independent benchmarks.

Benchmark-pooled capability vectors show an interior clustering optimum at a small number of clusters on all 12 evaluated models, contrasting with raw per-text vectors lacking natural cluster granularity.

Cross-benchmark transfer evaluation across twelve models revealed difference-in-means achieved the highest model-level mean on ten models, while logistic regression won the most capability-model cells, indicating readout method and aggregation criteria are significant evaluation dimensions.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a standardized, reusable framework for evaluating and comparing representation engineering methods in large language models, reducing reliance on paper-specific synthetic data.

papers.title: TriShield: Zero-Utility-Loss Defense Against Privacy Backdoors in Federated Language Model Fine-Tuning via Orthogonal Gradient Projection and Optimizer State Entanglement

summary.tldr: TriShield is a three-layer defense preventing privacy backdoors in federated LLM fine-tuning, achieving zero utility loss and 0% NeuroImprint reconstruction.
key_points: TriShield employs a Parameter Artifact Detector to identify memory-neuron signatures before local training.
A Stateful Virtual Iteration mechanism entangles Adam/AdamW's momentum state across virtual steps, invalidating NeuroImprint's inversion.
A Zero-Utility Orthogonal Projection operator eliminates gradient components carrying private memorization by projecting updates onto the main-task semantic subspace via SVD.
The defense theoretically proves zero mutual information between uploaded gradients and individual training samples after layers 2 and 3.
Experiments on GPT-2 (117M) and Llama-Guard-3-1B show TriShield reduces NeuroImprint reconstruction to 0% with less than 5% additional GPU overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: This defense enables secure federated fine-tuning of LLMs by completely preventing privacy backdoor attacks like NeuroImprint without compromising model utility or increasing communication rounds.

papers.title: TORUS: A Test of Rendering-Understanding Self-Coherence for Unified Audio Models

summary.tldr: TORUS introduces the first self-coherence benchmark for audio-native unified models, testing whether models can correctly understand and evaluate their own generated and edited audio across speech, sound, and music.
key_points: TORUS consists of 48 three-stage self-coherence tests with 432 six-option multiple-choice questions across five task families.
Evaluating five open unified models revealed that the top-performing model achieved 50.5% accuracy compared to a Cascaded Baseline's 63.2% and a 16.7% random chance floor.
Both specialized and unified audio models demonstrate limited self-coherence, with models struggling significantly on audio editing tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating self-coherence reveals functional disconnects between a unified model's generation and understanding capabilities that isolated task benchmarks fail to catch.

papers.title: To Add Is Machine, To Delete Is Human: Measuring and Mitigating Deletion Avoidance in LLM Code Editing

summary.tldr: LLMs display systematic deletion avoidance during code editing, underperforming on line-exact removals and passing tests by wrapping targeted code in guards rather than deleting it.
key_points: Leading SWE-bench Verified models achieve at most 71.7% deletion recall, failing to delete exact target lines in over 48% of cases despite reaching the correct file 92% of the time.
29.0% of passing patches exhibit Guard-and-Go behavior by wrapping targeted code in guards or fallbacks; retrofitting 34 tasks with deletion-checking tests dropped pass rates from 63.2% to 41.9%.
On CanItDelete, a new 200-task pure-deletion benchmark, the best model failed 20% of tasks while smaller open models dropped to an 18.0% success rate.

Prompting GPT-5.6 Sol with exact lines reduced incomplete deletion but capped success at 80.5% due to over-deletion or unnecessary additions; post-training targeted at deletion mitigated the bias and improved general editing.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on LLM-generated code edits degrades codebase maintainability because models bypass removing obsolete code, passing test suites while accumulating technical debt.

papers.title: Validation Evidence in LLM Repair Agents: How Much of What Passes Actually Tests the Bug?

summary.tldr: BSG-VA analysis reveals 46.0% of passing validation events in LLM repair agents lack bug-discriminating information, though returning buggy-state replay feedback significantly reduces evidence-inadequate closures.
key_points: BSG-VA evaluates validation events by replaying test-only patches against original buggy code (B), candidate state (S), and gold fix (G).

Analysis of 3,730 events across 643 rollouts showed 46.0% of positive comparable events were not bug-discriminating, and 23.8% of baseline rollouts closed based entirely on non-discriminating evidence.

Bug-contrast feedback (returning B-replay outcomes) reduced evidence-inadequate closures by 7.8 percentage points (p = 0.0029) and increased bug-discriminating evidence by 7.4 points (p = 0.011) without harming repair success.

An attention-matched reminder accounted for roughly one-third of the feedback's benefit, with B-replay content adding a detectable increment only when using gpt-5.6-sol in an unconstrained tool-use loop.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM repair agents frequently accept patches based on tests that fail to actually exercise the underlying bug, highlighting a need for stronger validation mechanisms like bug-contrast execution to prevent false-positive fixes.

papers.title: TextCloak: Thwarting Unauthorized LLM Exploitation via RL-Driven Unlearnable Text

summary.tldr: TextCloak is an RL-driven framework that generates unlearnable text perturbations to prevent unauthorized LLM fine-tuning while maintaining semantic fidelity and naturalness.
key_points: Uses a generative policy to transform clean text batches into unlearnable examples suitable for open-ended LLM generation tasks.
Introduces GRPO-UE, a group-relative policy optimization method that rewards the generator based on downstream performance degradation in fine-tuned surrogate LLMs.
Employs bi-level optimization to learn generalizable protective patterns rather than simple class-specific linguistic cues.
Validated across six public datasets and nine state-of-the-art LLMs, demonstrating transferability and resistance to adaptive attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a practical defense mechanism to protect proprietary text from being exploited for unauthorized LLM training without ruining text utility for legitimate users.

papers.title: Model or Harness? An Interaction-Centric Taxonomy for Localizing Agent Failures

summary.tldr: A new interaction-centric taxonomy localizes AI agent failures to 41 specific failure modes along component interaction edges, assigning fault to either the model, harness, environment, or evaluation grader to guide precise repairs.
key_points: Organizes 41 failure modes by mapping failures directly to the interaction edge between system components and determining the responsible fault side.
Distinguishes repair targets across four domains: model post-training, harness scaffolding, environment redesign, and benchmark/grader fixes.
Applies universally across diverse architectures including coding assistants, long-horizon personal assistants, and multi-agent systems.
Evaluated using LLMs as judges, with the strongest frontier model achieving Cohen's κ=0.76 agreement against human-annotated category labels.
summary.why_it_matters: By shifting failure analysis from outcome-level metrics to component-level fault attribution, developers can target interventions like harness fixes or model post-training without re-engineering the entire agent system.

papers.title: Benchmarks Are Not Monolithic: Sample-Level Auditing and Orchestration for LLM Evaluation

summary.tldr: A meta-evaluation framework audits LLM benchmarks at the sample level across five latent dimensions, enabling criterion-driven subset orchestration beyond monolithic aggregate accuracy scores.
key_points: Audits benchmarks across five latent dimensions: Cognitive/Knowledge Demands, Language/Content Quality, Task Properties, Context, and Ethics/Safety/Fairness.
Annotated five standard LLM benchmarks: MMLU, ARC, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, and TruthfulQA.
Reveals significant internal dataset heterogeneity that remains hidden when relying solely on aggregate accuracy metrics.
Enables criterion-driven re-composition of evaluation subsets tailored to specific capabilities like Reasoning Depth or Ethical Sensitivity.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows practitioners to decompose aggregate benchmark scores into targeted, fine-grained evaluations tailored to specific model capabilities and safety criteria.

papers.title: Conditioning Tree-Based Diffusions and Flows for Probabilistic Tabular Regression

summary.tldr: DiffGBM introduces a tree-based flow-matching framework and a tunable score-side space for tabular regression, replacing neural diffusion defaults with optimized gradient-boosted ensembles.
key_points: Formulates a Gaussian-path flow-matching trainer using LightGBM to directly learn velocity fields for p(y|x), enabling algebraic score recovery and few-step deterministic ODE sampling.
Exposes a score-flex space allowing joint tuning of residualization, EDM-style preconditioning, log-sigma time sampling, noise-level features, loss weighting, and histogram resolution.
Outperforms the standard published tree-based diffusion baseline across all 11 evaluated tabular benchmarks in paired Wilcoxon tests under a matched 40-trial tuning budget.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that default neural diffusion settings constrain tree-based generative models, providing a superior gradient-boosted method for probabilistic tabular regression.

papers.title: DeltaServe: Host-Agnostic Co-Serving of Inference and Fine-Tuning for LLMs

summary.tldr: DeltaServe is a host-agnostic co-serving system that uses an SLO-aware, CUDA-graph-aware scheduler to convert idle LLM inference capacity into LoRA fine-tuning throughput without violating latency targets.
key_points: Integrates with existing inference engines (such as vLLM, SGLang, and S-LoRA) via a compact hook interface requiring only multi-LoRA batching support.
Exploits shared execution structures between inference prefill and LoRA fine-tuning forward passes to execute fine-tuning when inference headroom exists.
Uses a latency model calibrated offline and refined online to dynamically govern fine-tuning admission based on strict inference SLOs.
Achieved 2.9x higher fine-tuning throughput than LLMStation at 100% SLO compliance (versus 85% for LLMStation) on a production trace using vLLM.
Outperformed a vLLM+torchtune baseline by 39% in fine-tuning throughput on identical hardware with zero SLO violations.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows operators to maximize hardware utilization and achieve significantly higher fine-tuning throughput on existing GPU clusters without degrading real-time inference latency.

papers.title: When Unlearning Fails: Reliable Data Deletion under Post-Training in Agent Networks

summary.tldr: MUTE addresses 'influence echoes' in self-improving federated agent networks, where deleted data's influence persists in retained trajectories, by using lightweight server ledgers, targeted updates, and trajectory quarantine.
key_points: In closed-loop federated agent networks, unlearning target data fails to stop 'influence echoes' that re-enter the network via retained trajectories shaped by the deleted data.
MUTE tracks downstream influence using a server ledger without requiring full network retraining.
The method mitigates echoes via a forget-retain update and contains high-influence retained trajectories through down-weighting or quarantine.
MUTE implements behavioral auditing to schedule extra erasure steps while constrained by an uplink communication budget.
Evaluated on LIBERO with two vision-language-action backbones and a physical Jetson edge testbed, MUTE reduced leakage and communication costs while preserving task utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables true privacy-compliant data deletion in continuously learning multi-agent systems without destroying model performance or requiring costly full retraining.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Skill Optimization

summary.tldr: Self-Supervised Skill Optimization (SSO) optimizes reusable agent skills using unlabeled task instances, generating skill probes and using an LLM judge to rank behavioral differences without ground-truth feedback.
key_points: Executes current skills on unlabeled batches to generate and run complete skill probes.
Employs an LLM judge to compare answers, trajectories, artifacts, or terminal states across executions.
Uses a separate behavior extractor to identify behavioral differences independently of the judge's choices.
Ranks extracted behaviors by aggregated evidence, renders a new skill from top behaviors, and validates it on an unlabeled validation set.
Approaches or exceeds ground-truth-based skill optimizers on closed-ended benchmarks and outperforms existing ground-truth-free prompt optimizers.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables continuous optimization of LLM agent procedural guidance in real-world domains where task labels, rewards, and evaluators are unavailable.

papers.title: Demystifying Entropy-based Selection for Chain-of-Thought Compression in Large Reasoning Models

summary.tldr: New empirical evaluation reveals entropy-based selection for Chain-of-Thought compression performs no better than random pruning, as semantic reasoning information is distributed across the full chain rather than concentrated in low-entropy tokens.
key_points: Entropy-based selection of low- or high-entropy sentence steps offers zero accuracy advantage over random pruning across models and reasoning tasks.
Low-entropy token retention appears effective on math benchmarks only because numeric tokens inherently carry low entropy while conveying critical task semantics.

Patching activations for a small subset of CoT tokens recovers near-perfect full-trace performance, showing task information is causally distributed across the entire CoT trace rather than isolated in heuristic-identified tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers cannot rely on entropy metrics to compress reasoning traces without losing critical context, requiring whole-chain compression strategies instead.

papers.title: TriShield: Zero-Utility-Loss Defense Against Privacy Backdoors in Federated Language Model Fine-Tuning via Orthogonal Gradient Projection and Optimizer State Entanglement

summary.tldr: TriShield is a three-layer deterministic defense against privacy backdoor attacks in federated LLM fine-tuning that eliminates private sample reconstruction without degrading model utility or requiring additional communication rounds.
key_points: Neutralizes NeuroImprint attacks, which exploit single-update memorization neurons in PEFT adapters to analytically reconstruct client training data with high semantic fidelity.
Combines three defense layers: Parameter Artifact Detection, Stateful Virtual Iteration (entangling Adam/AdamW momentum states), and Zero-Utility Orthogonal Projection via SVD.
Proves theoretically that the mutual information between uploaded local gradients and individual training samples is reduced to zero.
Demonstrates a 0% reconstruction rate on GPT-2 (117M) and Llama-Guard-3-1B with under 5% GPU computational overhead while preserving original training accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a computationally efficient mechanism to completely block privacy backdoor data reconstruction in federated LLM fine-tuning without trading off model accuracy.

papers.title: Agreement Is Not Quality: Blind Expert Verification of Human and LLM Qualitative Coding When Human Consensus Is Not Ground Truth

summary.tldr: A study shows human-LLM agreement metrics fail to capture qualitative coding quality, as blind expert verification found LLM coding equal or superior to human coders despite low Jaccard agreement scores.
key_points: Evaluated 5 LLM systems and 3 trained human coders applying a 72-item hierarchical codebook to 2,560 educator messages.

Human-LLM agreement (mean Jaccard 0.30) was lower than human-human agreement (0.52), but a blind domain expert preferred human over LLM code sets at statistically indistinguishable rates (51.5% vs. 48.5%, p = 0.537).
A Bradley-Terry ranking based on 855 blind pairwise comparisons placed two LLMs above two of the three human coders.
Human consensus exhibited shared bias for certain substantive codes that the expert verifier rejected in favor of LLM interpretations.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating LLMs solely on agreement with human coders misleads automation decisions by penalizing model outputs that correct for shared human bias.

papers.title: Fragility of Value under Imperfect Alignment

summary.tldr: A theoretical model demonstrates conditions where ideal alignment training produces agents with eta-catastrophic value functions that drive expected human value below eta under infinite optimization power.
key_points: Models ideal alignment training where an agent's value function must satisfy a proxy condition before deployment.
Proves that despite passing proxy checks, agents can harbor eta-catastrophic value functions that ruin expected human value at high optimization limits.
Identifies specific conditions relating human value functions to proxy condition accuracy that lead to deploying catastrophic agents.
Demonstrates the theoretical fragility of human value under overoptimization.
Advocates for architectures that cap optimization pressure, such as quantilizers, over exclusive reliance on pre-deployment validation.
summary.why_it_matters: Pre-deployment alignment testing cannot guarantee safety under heavy optimization, necessitating system designs that explicitly bound optimization power.

papers.title: WaiT for the Signal: Simple Frequency-Aware Flow-Matching

summary.tldr: WaiT introduces frequency-aware flow-matching that uses lossless wavelets to delay high-frequency generation until coarse structures emerge, reducing compute and improving pixel-space image and video quality.
key_points: Decomposes image generation into coarse and fine spatial frequency bands using lossless wavelets.
Delays high-frequency generation by keeping those bands as pure noise until coarse structures are established.
Reduces sampling compute by up to 50% while achieving a pixel-space FID of 1.43 on ImageNet 512x512.
Sets a pixel-space ImageNet 512x512 state-of-the-art FID of 1.3 with a 2B parameter model, and a Kinetics-600 FVD of 0.84 for video generation.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that frequency-aware scheduling in flow-matching models improves texture fidelity and fine detail while halving sampling compute costs across high-resolution image and video generation tasks.

papers.title: Agents That Certify Their Own Exploits: Confidence-Scheduled Restricted Responses for Safe Opponent Exploitation

summary.tldr: Confidence-Scheduled Restricted Responses (CS-RNR) is the first opponent-exploitation method in two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games that self-certifies safety by evaluating full-tree best responses against deployed strategies before commitment.
key_points: Tracks pooled action frequencies using anytime-valid confidence sequences, identifying deviations only when intervals separate from equilibrium references.
Solves restricted responses over a grid of pin levels from conservative opponent models, evaluating each candidate via a full-tree best response.
Compares compute-generated certificates against a user-specified loss budget to execute atomic strategy commitments.
Outperformed a money-verified binary gate in Leduc hold'em by achieving 6.2x steady-state gain, with trajectory mixtures reaching 13.6x.
Empirically validated across Leduc, Liar's Dice, and 5-rank Leduc, with all 36,000 audited hands adhering to certificate tolerances.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows agents to safely exploit imperfect opponents without risking high exploitability, guaranteeing that every deployed strategy adheres to strict, self-audited loss bounds.

papers.title: TCA-SIR: Learning Target-Conditioned Abstractions for Scientific Inspiration Retrieval

summary.tldr: TCA-SIR reformulates Scientific Inspiration Retrieval by generating target-conditioned abstract principles from candidate papers to predict transferability instead of relying on topical similarity.
key_points: Replaces standard topical similarity ranking with target-conditioned abstraction (TCA) to evaluate how candidate inspirations transfer to a target problem.
Extracts transferable abstract principles from candidates specifically framed for the target to represent reusable problem-solving mechanisms.
Outperforms prior methods and direct LLM retrieval on ResearchBench, exceeding MOOSE-Chem's HitRate@top4% by over 10 percentage points.
Provides interpretable rationales by recovering target-relevant mechanisms better than untrained TCA prompts.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the retrieval of remote, cross-domain scientific inspirations by evaluating functional transferability rather than surface-level topical overlap.

security.title: A hole in every one: bypassing the open source AI skill scanners

summary.tldr: Adversa AI evaluated eight open-source AI skill scanners against real-world attacks and found that a malicious skill successfully bypassed all of them.
key_points: Eight open-source AI skill scanners were tested against real attacks.
A malicious skill successfully bypassed all eight evaluated scanners.
The bypassed security tools included the top-ranked scanner on the current OASB leaderboard.
summary.why_it_matters: Current open-source scanners for AI agent skills fail to detect real-world attacks, leaving systems vulnerable to malicious code.

security.title: Hollow-LLM Attack: Computationally Trivial Weights in Zero-Knowledge Verification of LLM Inference

summary.tldr: The Hollow-LLM attack exploits an effort gap in zero-knowledge LLM inference verification, allowing providers to use ghost weights that collapse computation to a fraction of the cost while producing valid proofs of correct execution.
key_points: Zero-knowledge LLM inference proves equational correctness under committed weights but fails to bind the computational effort required to generate the output.
The Hollow-LLM attack embeds algebraically structured ghost weights into standard transformer blocks within the declared architecture and parameter count.
Provers can reduce serving costs to match much smaller models with zero quality loss while still satisfying the verification circuit.
summary.why_it_matters: Proof of correct execution in zero-knowledge LLM inference does not guarantee that a provider actually performed the computational workload of a large model, enabling dishonest cost savings.

security.title: TextCloak: Thwarting Unauthorized LLM Exploitation via RL-Driven Unlearnable Text

summary.tldr: TextCloak uses a generative reinforcement learning framework driven by GRPO-UE to create unlearnable text perturbations that prevent unauthorized fine-tuning of Large Language Models while maintaining semantic fidelity.
key_points: Replaces class-specific classification shortcuts with a generative policy trained via Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO-UE) for open-ended text generation.
Utilizes bi-level optimization where policy rewards are calculated based on utility degradation in fine-tuned surrogate LLMs.
Validated across six datasets and nine modern LLM architectures to verify defense utility against adaptive attacks.
Preserves text naturalness and semantic accuracy for legitimate uses while degrading unauthorized fine-tuning capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables content creators to safeguard open-ended textual data against unauthorized LLM scraping and fine-tuning without rendering the text unreadable to humans.

security.title: Emerging Challenges in Threat Modeling for GenAI-Augmented Systems: A View from the Trenches

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated three GenAI-aware threat modeling methods on an industrial SME case study, revealing significant gaps in identifying GenAI supply chain and human-centered security risks.
key_points: Evaluated three GenAI-aware threat modeling methods selected via rapid literature review on an SME industrial system.
Traditional frameworks like STRIDE fail to capture emerging GenAI-specific risks.
Current GenAI threat modeling methods show limited coverage for software supply chain risks and human-centered security issues.
Practitioners reported usability challenges, high perceived effort, and integration barriers within SME development workflows.
summary.why_it_matters: Existing GenAI threat modeling tools leave critical gaps in supply chain and human-centered security, requiring SME-friendly frameworks to effectively secure AI-augmented software.

security.title: Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced a stealthy concurrent audio prompt injection attack that hides malicious instructions within user speech, along with the AudioAgentSecurity benchmark and the Cascaded Audio Decoupling and Verification (CADV) defense mechanism.
key_points: The attack uses instruction augmentation and scenario concealment to piggyback malicious audio instructions onto benign user speech, achieving a 69.10% average Attack Success Rate against Gemini 3 Pro.

AudioAgentSecurity was constructed as the first benchmark for audio instruction injection, featuring 8 real-world task scenarios and 10 attack patterns evaluated across 11 agents including GPT-4o-audio.
CADV defends against attacks by combining source separation and consistency analysis, achieving up to 96% detection accuracy.
Real-world validity was verified using human volunteers and the Doubao AI Smartphone in dynamic environment scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: Multimodal LLM agents accepting continuous audio inputs are vulnerable to covert hijackings through ambient audio, requiring specialized acoustic source separation defenses beyond prompt-level filtering.

security.title: Benign on Label, Malicious by Design: Clean-Label Dormant-to-Activated Backdoor via Machine Unlearning with Removable Camouflage

summary.tldr: A clean-label backdoor framework uses dual-generator learning and bilevel optimization to keep backdoors dormant until a small subset of camouflage samples is removed via machine unlearning.
key_points: Formulates clean-label backdoor injection as a bilevel optimization problem using dual-generator learning.
Alternately learns sample-specific triggers for latent associations and label-consistent camouflage samples for removable suppression.
Activates the dormant backdoor once a small subset of suppressive camouflage samples is unlearned by the model.
Demonstrates lower pre-unlearning Attack Success Rates (ASR) and higher post-unlearning activation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-10 compared to existing baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that machine unlearning can be exploited as an activation trigger for hidden backdoors, creating security risks for models complying with data removal requests.

security.title: Don't Trust the AI Ecosystem: Analyzing Privacy Leakage in Compromised Open-Source Components

summary.tldr: GradLock is a training-time injection attack that covertly embeds training data into model parameters, enabling near-lossless extraction from compromised open-source components without post-training optimization.
key_points: Uses stateless deterministic indexing to create isolated data vaults within model parameters.
Employs dynamic gradient locking to prevent payload degradation during training and optimize retention against quantization, pruning, and fine-tuning.
Reconstructs target training images with near-lossless quality (SSIM ~ 1.0) and instant extraction times under 1.0 second on MNIST, Imagenette, and CelebA.
Defeats human inspection, with 93.3% of deployment study participants failing to detect the injected malicious logic.
summary.why_it_matters: This vulnerability demonstrates that compromised open-source AI supply chains can be exploited to exfiltrate exact training data, bypassing standard post-training security defenses and detection.

vendors.title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT-5.6

summary.tldr: OpenAI announces lower GPT-5.6 pricing for Luna and Terra, enabling more efficient AI workflow deployment for enterprises.
key_points: Lower GPT-5.6 pricing for Luna.
Lower GPT-5.6 pricing for Terra.
OpenAI's models are more efficient.
Enables enterprises to deploy AI workflows at scale.
summary.why_it_matters: Reduced pricing and increased efficiency for GPT-5.6 models facilitate broader enterprise adoption of AI workflows.

summary.tldr: The llm-chat-completions-server 0.1a0 plugin enables LLM models to serve OpenAI Chat Completion style requests, leveraging content-addressable logs for conversation state de-duplication.
key_points: The plugin supports OpenAI Chat Completion style requests, where each incoming message extends the previous conversation.
It utilizes content-addressable logs from LLM 0.32rc1 to de-duplicate conversation messages using hashes of individual parts.
The server runs on a specified port (e.g., 9001) and exposes all installed LLM models via a ChatGPT Completions compatible endpoint.
Installation involves `uv tool install llm --pre`, `llm install llm-chat-completions-server`, and `llm chat-completions-server -p 9001`.
summary.why_it_matters: This allows LLM models to integrate seamlessly with systems expecting the OpenAI Chat Completions API, simplifying development and deployment.

summary.tldr: LLM 0.32rc1 introduces a new schema for prompt/response details, utilizing content-addressable hash IDs for message de-duplication and supporting forked conversations, alongside new model support.
key_points: New schema design improves capture of prompt and response details for current model families.
Content-addressable hash IDs are implemented for stored messages, enabling database de-duplication.
The update allows LLM to represent trees of messages for forked conversations.
Support for gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, and gpt-5.6-luna models has been added.
A significant schema change involves new tables; existing data is unaffected, but a logs.db backup is recommended.
summary.why_it_matters: This release enhances LLM's ability to manage and track complex conversational data structures and integrates with newer language models.
